title: What Time Should I Go to Bed? Sleep Cycles Explained
seoTitle: What Time Should I Go to Bed? Sleep Cycle Bedtimes Explained
excerpt: How sleep cycles work, how to work out a bedtime from your alarm, and simple habits for falling asleep on time.
description: How to work out the best time to go to bed from your wake-up time using 90-minute sleep cycles, with example bedtimes and tips for falling asleep on time.
body:
If you've ever woken up groggy after a long sleep, or surprisingly fresh after a short one, sleep cycles may be part of the reason. Here's how they work and how to use them to choose a bedtime.

## What is a sleep cycle?

During the night your sleep moves through stages: light sleep, deep sleep and REM sleep, when most dreaming happens. One trip through these stages is a sleep cycle. A cycle takes roughly 90 minutes on average, though it varies from person to person and through the night. Most adults go through four to six cycles a night.

Waking at the end of a cycle, when sleep is lighter, often feels easier than being woken from deep sleep.

## How much sleep do adults need?

Most adults need about 7 to 9 hours a night. In cycles, that's usually 5 cycles (7.5 hours) or 6 cycles (9 hours).

## Work out your bedtime from your alarm

Count back from your wake-up time in 90-minute steps, then allow about 15 minutes to fall asleep.

If your alarm is set for **7:00 am**:

- **6 cycles (9 hours):** go to bed at about **9:45 pm**
- **5 cycles (7.5 hours):** go to bed at about **11:15 pm**
- **4 cycles (6 hours):** go to bed at about **12:45 am**, fine for one night but not every night

Try your own times in the free [sleep calculator](/tools/sleep-calculator/). It works it out both ways: a bedtime for your alarm, or a wake-up time if you go to bed now.

## Treat it as a guide, not a rule

Cycle length isn't exactly 90 minutes for everyone, and it changes during the night. Use the calculator as a starting point, then adjust by 15 minutes or so until you find a time that leaves you feeling rested.

## Habits that make the bedtime work

- **Keep the same wake-up time every day,** including weekends. It's one of the most effective ways to steady your body clock.
- **Wind down for 30 to 60 minutes** before bed: dim lights, put screens away and do something calm.
- **Cut caffeine after early afternoon.** Its effects can last for hours.
- **Keep your bedroom cool, dark and quiet.**
- **If you can't sleep after about 20 minutes,** get up and do something relaxing in low light, then go back to bed when you feel sleepy.

If poor sleep goes on for weeks or affects your day, speak to a doctor.

SleepWise builds on this with a sleep diary and a personal sleep plan based on CBT-I, the structured approach to better sleep that many sleep specialists recommend.
